en.name: Pork rinds
en.summary: A bag of pork rinds keeps 4 months from the date of manufacture, stored sealed in a cool, dry cupboard. They are puffed, fried pork skin — dry, salty and almost pure protein and fat — so the clock is the fat going rancid rather than anything growing.
en.pantry: 4 months from the date of manufacture, which is the date to look for on the bag rather than the day you bought it. Sealed, cool, dark and dry is all they ask. Frying drives the water out of the skin, and what is left has no free moisture for bacteria to use; the limit is oxidation of the pork fat, which warmth and light both speed up. An opened bag also goes soft quickly, because salt and puffed protein together pull moisture out of the air, so clip it hard or decant into an airtight tub.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is published. Pork rinds do not need refrigeration and the fridge is a humid place, so a bag left in there loses its crackle within a day or two. Cold would in principle slow the fat down, but the trade is a bad one: you gain a little on rancidity and lose the texture, which is the entire point of the food.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published either. Freezing does no harm — there is almost no water in a pork rind to form ice — but the cupboard figure is already generous for a snack, and condensation on the way out will soften them unless the container is fully sealed and allowed to warm before opening.
en.thawing: Not normally applicable. If a bag has been chilled or frozen, let it come back to room temperature sealed before you open it.
spoilage: A smell of old cooking oil, crayons or paint — rancid pork fat.
Rinds that bend and chew instead of shattering.
A yellowing, greasy look on what should be pale and dry.
Any sour or off smell on opening the bag.
tips: Look for the manufacture date on the bag; the clock starts there, not at purchase.
Clip an opened bag or tip it into an airtight tub — salt pulls moisture from the air.
Keep them away from the hob; heat is what turns the fat.
A minute or two in a hot oven re-crisps rinds that have gone soft, though it will not fix rancidity.

faq.q: How long do pork rinds keep?
faq.a: 4 months from the date of manufacture, sealed in a cool, dry cupboard.

faq.q: Do pork rinds need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: No, and no refrigerated timeline is published. The fridge is humid and would cost you the crackle without buying much.

faq.q: How can you tell if pork rinds have gone bad?
faq.a: Smell the bag. Rancid pork fat smells of old oil or crayons. Softness on its own is just moisture.

zh.name: 炸豬皮
zh.summary: 一包炸豬皮自「製造日期」起可放 4 個月，密封放在陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃。它是膨發油炸的豬皮——又乾又鹹，幾乎只有蛋白質和脂肪——所以倒數的是油脂油耗，而不是什麼東西在生長。
zh.pantry: 自製造日期起 4 個月；要看的是包裝上的製造日期，而不是你買回來那天。密封、陰涼、避光、乾燥，它的要求就這些。油炸把豬皮裡的水趕了出去，剩下的東西沒有自由水可以讓細菌利用；限制它的是豬油氧化，而溫度和光線都會加速。開封後它也會很快變軟，因為鹽加上膨發的蛋白質很會把空氣裡的水吸過來，所以請把袋口夾緊，或倒進氣密盒。
zh.fridge: 沒有冷藏的期限數據。炸豬皮不需要冷藏，而冰箱又潮濕，放進去一兩天就沒有那個「喀」聲了。低溫理論上能拖慢油脂變化，但這個交換很不划算：你在油耗上賺一點，卻賠掉整個食物的重點——口感。
zh.freezer: 冷凍同樣沒有期限數據。凍了不會壞——炸豬皮裡幾乎沒有水可以結冰——但櫥櫃的期限對一份零食來說已經很夠；而且除非容器完全密封並且回溫後才打開，拿出來時的結露都會讓它變軟。
zh.thawing: 一般用不到。若冰過或凍過，請維持密封回到室溫再打開。
spoilage: 聞起來像久放的食用油、蠟筆或油漆——那是豬油油耗。
咬下去是彎的、韌的，而不是碎裂開來。
本來乾爽淡色的表面變得泛黃、油膩。
開袋時有任何酸味或怪味。
tips: 看包裝上的製造日期，計時是從那裡開始，不是從你買回來開始。
開封後夾緊或倒進氣密盒——鹽會把空氣裡的水吸過來。
遠離爐台；讓油脂走味的就是熱。
軟掉的話，高溫烤箱烘一兩分鐘可以回脆，但救不了油耗味。

faq.a: 自製造日期起 4 個月，密封放陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃。
不需要，而且它沒有冷藏的期限數據。冰箱潮濕，會讓你賠掉口感又換不到多少。
聞袋子。豬油油耗會有久放的油味或蠟筆味。單純變軟只是受潮。
